conditions.description: The email input has no label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or other explicit accessible name in the supplied markup.
conditions.rationale: Placeholder-free unlabeled form controls create a direct accessible-name defect visible in static markup.

conditions.description: The validation error is revealed visually but is not associated with the email field and has no live-region semantics for announcement.
conditions.rationale: The supplied markup and script expose the error without aria-describedby, role=alert, or aria-live.

conditions.description: The page declares a language and uses a native h1, form, and submit button; these are negative controls against inventing missing-language or non-semantic-button defects.
conditions.rationale: The relevant semantics are explicitly present in the fixture.

conditions.description: Actual screen-reader announcement behavior across browser and assistive-technology combinations cannot be established from source alone.
conditions.rationale: Observed assistive-technology behavior requires runtime evidence not included in this fixture.

conditions.description: Accessibility readiness must not be cleared while the form lacks an accessible name/error relationship or runtime AT behavior remains unverified.
conditions.rationale: Static markup can establish some defects but cannot establish complete end-user accessibility.
